title: Regulator assistance to the Board
mainQuestion: How may a regulator assist the Energy and Utilities Board without becoming a party?
studySummary: For section 49.1, regulator has the meaning from the Financial and Consumer Services Commission Act. On application of the Board after a proceeding begins from financial and consumer services legislation, a regulator who is not already a party may assist the Board without becoming a party. The Board may receive and accept relevant information from that regulator whether or not it would be admissible in court.

title: Supervisor hazard, information, and instruction duties
mainQuestion: What specific hazard, information, and instruction duties does subsection 9.1(2) impose on supervisors?
studySummary: Without limiting the general duties in subsection 9.1(1), every supervisor has three specific duties for employees under the supervisor supervision and direction: acquaint them with hazards connected to listed workplace things and agents, provide information necessary for their health and safety, and provide instruction necessary for their health and safety.

title: Unregistered instrument consequences
mainQuestion: What are the consequences of not registering instruments for purchasers and judgment creditors under section 19?
studySummary: Instruments may be registered in the county registry office where the lands lie. Subject to the listed timing exceptions in later subsections, unregistered instruments are deemed fraudulent and void against subsequent purchasers for valuable consideration whose conveyances are previously registered. Instruments not registered within three months after execution are also deemed fraudulent and void against a bona fide judgment creditor if the judgment or memorial was registered before the conveyance was registered.

objectives.guidedQuestion: What happens to an unregistered instrument against a subsequent purchaser?
objectives.studyAnswer: Subject to subsections 19(3), (4), (4.1), and (5), an instrument not registered in the county registry office where the lands lie is deemed fraudulent and void against subsequent purchasers for valuable consideration whose conveyances are previously registered.

evidence.evidenceText: shall, subject to the provisions of subsections (3), (4), (4.1) and (5), be deemed fraudulent and void against subsequent purchasers for valuable consideration whose conveyances are previously registered

objectives.objective: Recall the judgment-creditor consequence and timing.
objectives.guidedQuestion: When is an instrument deemed fraudulent and void against a bona fide judgment creditor?
objectives.studyAnswer: Subject to subsections 19(3), (4), (4.1), and (5), if an instrument is not registered within three months of execution, it is deemed fraudulent and void against a bona fide judgment creditor when the judgment or memorial was registered before the conveyance was registered.

title: Registration timing exceptions for leases, sales, and wills
mainQuestion: What registration timing exceptions protect certain leases, sale conveyances, and wills under section 19?
studySummary: Section 19 carves out several timing rules from the general non-registration consequences. Short leases of not more than three years with actual possession do not need registration merely to avoid being fraudulent and void. Official public-auction conveyances and sheriff sale conveyances receive protected validity if registered within six months. A will is protected if registered within six months after death when the testator died in the Province, or within one year after death when the testator died outside the Province.

objectives.objective: Recall the short-lease exception.
objectives.guidedQuestion: Which leases need not be registered merely to avoid being fraudulent and void?
objectives.studyAnswer: A lease for a term not exceeding three years need not be registered, and is not deemed fraudulent and void merely for non-registration, if actual possession goes along with the lease; this does not apply to leases over three years or leases without actual possession.

evidence.evidenceText: No lease for a term not exceeding three years, where the actual possession goes along with the lease, need be registered

objectives.objective: Recall the official public-auction conveyance timing rule.
objectives.guidedQuestion: When is an official-capacity public-auction conveyance protected as if registered at the time of sale?
objectives.studyAnswer: When a person in an official capacity executes a conveyance of an interest in lands sold at public auction pursuant to law, the conveyance is as valid against subsequent purchasers or judgment creditors as if registered at the time of sale if registered within six months of the day of sale.

evidence.evidenceText: if registered within six months of the day of such sale, shall, as against any subsequent purchaser or judgment creditor, be as valid as if registered at the time of sale

objectives.objective: Recall the sheriff sale conveyance timing rule.
objectives.guidedQuestion: When is a sheriff sale conveyance protected as if registered on its execution day?
objectives.studyAnswer: If a sheriff executes a conveyance of an interest in lands sold under the Enforcement of Money Judgments Act, it is as valid against subsequent purchasers or judgment creditors as if registered on the day of execution if registered within six months after the day of execution.

evidence.evidenceText: if registered within six months after the day of its execution, shall, as against any subsequent purchaser or judgment creditor, be as valid as if registered on the day of its execution

objectives.objective: Recall the will registration timing rule.
objectives.guidedQuestion: When is a registered will protected as if registered immediately after death?
objectives.studyAnswer: A will is as valid against subsequent purchasers or judgment creditors as if registered immediately after death if registered within six months after death when the testator died in the Province, or within one year after death when the testator died outside the Province.

evidence.evidenceText: A will registered within six months after the death of the testator if he died within the Province, or within one year after death if he died without the Province

title: Transfer affidavit and forwarding requirement
mainQuestion: What affidavit must accompany a deed transferring real property, and what must the registrar do with it?
studySummary: A deed affecting transfer of real property cannot be registered unless it is accompanied by an affidavit of transfer. The affidavit must set out true and actual consideration, party names, location and description of the real property, and prescribed information; it is made by the grantee, the grantee solicitor, or another authorized agent, in the regulatory form or like effect. The registrar must not record the affidavit, but must forward it to the Executive Director of Assessment within thirty days after registration of the deed.

title: Boundary-confirmation application form and plan requirements
mainQuestion: What form and current-plan requirements apply to a boundary-confirmation application under Regulation 95-166?
studySummary: An application to confirm a boundary under subsection 6(1) or 6(3) of the Boundaries Confirmation Act must be in Form 1. The required plan of survey under paragraph 7(1)(a) of the Act must be current and must conform in every respect to the Association of New Brunswick Land Surveyors standards in effect when the application is made and to any other requirements specified by the Registrar General.

title: Boundary-confirmation application materials and surveyor report
mainQuestion: What materials and surveyor-report content must accompany a boundary-confirmation application?
studySummary: In addition to the plan of survey, an application to confirm a boundary must include field notes and a conforming surveyor report, available existing plans and related field notes or reports, required registered instruments, any requested abstract of title, owner and interest-holder mailing information, any consents, waivers, or agreements to be bound, and other helpful or requested information. The surveyor report must describe the issue, boundary history, evidence used for the shown boundary, and reasons for accepting or rejecting other indicated boundary locations.
